resale_co.name: Certificate of Habitability for Resale (certificate of occupancy for a new owner)
resale_co.issued_by: Hardyston Township Fire Prevention Bureau (Hardyston Fire Marshal) under a shared service agreement; the Borough Code assigns the certificate of occupancy to the Sussex Borough Zoning Officer
resale_co.lead_time: Hardyston contacts the applicant within a few business days to schedule. Sussex non-rushed inspections are Wednesdays 8 to 9 am and Thursdays 1 to 3 pm; rushed inspections can be outside those windows. The Borough Code says a certificate of occupancy is granted or denied within 15 days of a written application.
resale_co.valid_for: Inspections are good for 6 months (Hardyston application page)
requirements: Resale inspection through the Hardyston Fire Marshal before the new owner occupies
Smoke alarms on each level and outside each sleeping area; 10-year sealed battery units unless hardwired
Carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas where there is a fuel-burning device or attached garage
Warning label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter if the home has a generator, solar panels or battery storage
All construction permits must be closed with the Construction Department

fees.label: Certificate of habitability (COH) resale, each dwelling unit, request at least 10 business days before change of occupancy (Borough Code 24-1.5i3)
fees.quote: If request made at least 10 business days prior to change of occupancy: $50.

fees.label: COH resale, request 4 to 10 business days before change of occupancy (Borough Code)
fees.quote: If request made at least 10 business days but more than 4 business days prior to change of occupancy: $85.

fees.label: COH resale, request less than 4 business days before change of occupancy (Borough Code)
fees.quote: If request made less than 4 business days prior to change of occupancy: $150.

fees.quote: $100.00 - More than 10 business days prior to closing

fees.quote: $200.00 - Less than 4 business days prior to closing.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Use the Certificate of Habitability Resale link on the Borough's Zoning/Housing page, which opens the Hardyston Fire Prevention Bureau's online form (Sussex and Wantage - CSACMAPFEC). Enter owner, closing date, occupant, address and block/lot, and pay online. Paper applications can be picked up at the Hardyston Township Municipal Building Construction Office window, 149 Wheatsworth Road, Hardyston.

resale_co.notes: Borough Code 12-1.6b (read through the ecode360 print view) requires a certificate of occupancy before a new owner occupies an existing building, and the fee chapter still lists Certificate of Habitability resale fees of $50/$85/$150. The Borough's Zoning/Housing page now says all resale inspections are done through the Hardyston Fire Marshal, and its Certificate of Habitability Resale link opens Hardyston's smoke/CO certificate (CSACMAPFEC) form with fees of $100/$150/$200. So in practice the resale certificate and the smoke/CO certificate appear to be one Hardyston inspection, and the posted Hardyston fees, not the older Code fees, are what is charged. The Hardyston form is a JavaScript payment page, so a script may not be able to read its text. Rental units need an annual rental certificate of occupancy ($50 per unit) and landlord registration; rental-only.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area (NFPA 72); not required to be interconnected, but hardwired interconnected alarms from construction must stay that way
10-year sealed battery smoke alarms (ANSI/UL 217); A/C powered alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarms (UL 2034) in the immediate vicinity of sleeping areas where there is a fuel-burning device or attached garage

Secondary power source warning label (for example "CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER.") within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter if the home has a permanent generator, solar panels or battery storage
All construction permits must be closed with the Construction Department
No portable fire extinguisher is required

authorities.lead_time: Fee tiers count business days before closing: more than 10 business days for the lowest fee. Sussex non-rushed inspections are Wednesdays 8 to 9 am and Thursdays 1 to 3 pm. Inspections are good for 6 months.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply and pay online through the Hardyston Fire Prevention Bureau portal (Sussex and Wantage - CSACMAPFEC form). A representative contacts you by phone or email to schedule. Paper applications are at the Hardyston Township Municipal Building Construction Office window. A failed inspection needs a new request and a $50.00 re-inspection fee.

fire_cert.notes: Hardyston's posted rules say a portable fire extinguisher is no longer required, in line with P.L.2025, c.19. The fee and schedule text comes from Hardyston's online payment page (Tyler portal), which is built with JavaScript, so a script may not read it; the same rules also appear in Hardyston's posted regulations PDF. Note the inspection windows say non-rushed is "more than 5 days" while the fee tiers use 10 business days.

other_items.label: Sewer discharge certificate of compliance
other_items.detail: Before title transfers on any property with a building connected to the Borough sewer, the owner must get a certificate of compliance from the Zoning Officer (no prohibited discharges such as sump pumps or roof drains into the sanitary sewer). Inspection fee $50, paid before the inspection, on a Borough form.

other_items.label: Open construction permits
other_items.detail: All construction permits must be closed with the Construction Department (Hardyston Building Department, which runs the Borough's construction office) before the smoke/resale certificate.
